text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Lennart Meri held a news conference in the toilet after returning from Japan at Tallinn Airport toilet to point out the unsatisfactory state of the facilities.
- Lieutenant Colonel Lui Jaanson was appointed the new head of the Defence League.

- A European Commission poll reveals that the Estonians are among the most optimistic among the European nations about their future. Their attitude towards the European Union, however, is predominantly indifferent or negative.
- The city government of the southern town of Tartu may have to resign as the Reform Party faction is negotiating with others to remove the Fatherland Union from power.
- AN Estonian-Finnish visa-free travel agreement was signed in Tallinn.
- The president's advisor, Rain Rosimannus, will resign and will become an advisor of the Reform Party.
- The General Staff announced that eight countries, including the USA, will be represented in the peacekeeping exercise Baltic Challenge to be held in Estonia in July.
- Three investors, Arbolana, Baltic Cresco and ESCO Holding, compete for the privatisation of the Estonian Shipping Company.
- New requirements will make the qualification for a driving licence harder than before. The requirements are aimed at improving safety.
- Tallinn Police held a major raid in central Tallinn, detaining a number of persons suspected of theft.
